genre_note:
214 notes, 716 block assignments, 0 duplicate (doc, block) pairs, 95.5% of 48,728 words assigned, no note over the 1,800-word ceiling (max 561w, xbox_elite_wireless_controller_series_2).

CLUSTER SHAPE. c29 is not one topic; it is five genres wearing the same category label. (1) Longform reported feature — doc_0115, "The people who ruined the internet," 8,486 words, 17% of the cluster on its own, decomposed into 27 notes across three sub-plans. (2) Policy/legal news — AI regulation (0312, 0313), platform regulation (0498, 0505), Epic v. Google (0299, 0355). (3) Reviews and buying guides (0077, 0229, 0350). (4) Essay/analysis (0234, 0190, 0346). (5) Commerce roundups (0250, 0567, 0595, 0090, 0575) plus a newsletter (0607) — 16,375 words, a third of the cluster, and the place where "size before coherence" would have done the most damage.

BUILDING-BLOCK DISTRIBUTION AND ABSENCES. empirical_observation ~150 notes and concept ~22 dominate, exactly as the brief predicts for news. argument (12) and counter_argument (14) are real, not manufactured: news writing carries them wherever a claim meets a rebuttal — Google's "search hasn't declined" against the reporter's evidence; the SEOs who agree with Google against their own interest; Ofcom's rules against Wikimedia's nonprofit-capacity objection and against X's moderation rollback; Schumer arguing the EO does not go far enough; Molden warning that cutting tire wear mass could raise toxicity; the Elite Series 2's quality-control reputation inside a positive recommendation; the four VPNs that missed the cut. model (10) is reserved for genuine mechanism/causal chains: PageRank's link economy, the SEO-update arms cycle, E-E-A-T shifting search toward institutional authority, 6PPD reacting with ozone to make 6PPD-quinone that kills coho salmon, the attention economy's dopamine loop, Epic/Google's market-definition logic. procedure (8) covers real ordered steps and policy mechanics — the EO's reporting-and-red-team pipeline, the watermarking effort, Ofcom's codes, Discord's graduated warnings, Engadget's VPN test protocol, the controller evaluation rubric, driver actions that cut tire pollution, a five-app writing rotation.

hypothesis is genuinely rare and I did not manufacture it: only 3 notes, each a stated, falsifiable forward claim rather than a report of one — Daron Babin's prediction that free generative AI will flood search faster than Google can respond; the reporter's own speculation that anger at search results is displaced anger at the internet generally; the M1-to-M2-to-M3 cadence inference. Apple's rumor coverage otherwise reads as empirical_observation (Kuo said X, Gurman reported Y on date Z), not prediction, and I classified it that way. navigation: none produced, as instructed.

ENTITY SHARING (Step 3). 25 notes draw on more than one document, which is where the cluster's multi-hop value lives. Cross-document notes: amazon_october_prime_big_deal_days_2023 (0250+0567+0595), sony_wf_1000xm5 (0595+0250+0567), roku_streaming_stick_and_express_4k (0250+0567+0090), microsd_card_recommendations_and_deals (0250+0567+0090), plus 21 more spanning two docs each — apple_airpods_pro, bose_quietcomfort_earbuds_ii, bose_quietcomfort_45, google_pixel_buds_pro, beats_studio_pro, anker_soundcore_space_a40, shokz_openrun_pro, hyperx_cloud_gaming_headsets, logitech_g535, samsung_galaxy_watch_6, hisense_u6k_and_u8k, irobot_roomba_694, crucial_mx500, google_nest_cam, amazon_fire_tv_stick_4k, anker_511_nano_3_charger, tekton_everybit_tech_rescue_kit, epicka_universal_travel_adapter, chomchom_pet_hair_remover, and on the legal side epic_fortnite_project_liberty_payment_bypass, epic_antitrust_claims_against_google_play, google_defense_android_competes_with_ios, google_chat_auto_deletion_and_sanctions (all 0299+0355). The Prime Day trio in particular describes the same sale three times from three angles (day-one roundup, day-after leftovers, headphone-category deep dive); writing a Sony WF-1000XM5 note per document would have split that evidence three ways and lost all three.

COHERENCE OVER SIZE. The five commerce roundups are each one document but dozens of unrelated products. I split them per product (or per tight product family: item trackers, phone grips/cables, microSD cards, portable Bluetooth speakers), never per word budget. doc_0575's staff-favorites piece became 20 notes across two sub-plans; its per-item staff attributions (Alex Cranz, Victoria Song, Sean Hollister, etc.) were ASSIGNED, not dropped as bylines, because who recommended what is the document's organizing fact. doc_0115 was split at narrative/argumentative seams (the party, each practitioner's arc, each mechanism, each side of the quality debate), not at 1,800-word marks.

DROPPED CHROME, AND THE TWO CORRECTIONS I KEPT. Dropped: article titles (carried in the H1), section and product-name headers, photo/screenshot credits, affiliate disclosures, "Read our full review of X" and "Read next" links, newsletter signup boxes and merch promos, "Your October Prime Day Shopping Guide" footers, and pull-quotes that duplicate adjacent body text verbatim (doc_0115 blocks 14/36/49/61/74/87/100; doc_0190 blocks 5/10/19/29/38/47; doc_0498 blocks 3/9/13). Both update notices that read like routine corrections were ASSIGNED, because each states a scope condition on its own article: doc_0229[87] removes PPTP from the guide because Consumer Reports says the protocol "has serious security flaws" (folded into what_a_vpn_is_and_what_it_does_not_hide, which is where protocol quality is discussed), and doc_0505[17] retracts the claim that Discord would auto-DELETE sensitive content from strangers — the article's own headline promise — leaving only blurring (folded into discord_teen_safety_assist). doc_0355[5], the December 15th "It's basically over now" update, is likewise assigned to epic_v_google_trial_overview, since it contradicts the present tense of the whole explainer.

COVERAGE HONESTY. Every document lands at 91% or above. Weakest three, all for genre reasons rather than omission: doc_0607 (Installer newsletter) 91.0% — the discarded 234 words are the welcome, the "forward this to a friend / subscribe" plug, the embedded signup form, section labels, and an issue table-of-contents naming Valve/Humane/ChatGPT items that the text never elaborates; doc_0355 (Epic explainer) 91.0% — written as ~15 FAQ question headers plus author asides, all dropped as headers; doc_0595 (headphone deals) 92.3% — 33 dropped blocks are brand headers and one-line product-name headers, while every price card and every description is assigned. doc_0250 (92.5%), doc_0090 (92.9%) and doc_0567 (93.8%) lose the same way. No substantive claim was dropped anywhere; the shortfall is entirely publisher furniture.
